title: Choose the visual world for Softlligence
question: The roll assigned The Multi-Part Form Set: four plies for four products. Keep it, take the pick, or re-roll.

options.label: The Multi-Part Form Set
options.lineage: carbonless NCR forms: purchase orders, waybills, delivery notes in white, canary, pink and goldenrod plies
options.thesis: Softlligence sells four products, ERP, CRM, MIS and Inventory. The homepage is one printed form set: four plies, one per product, written once and read through every copy. It is the paperwork every operations buyer already trusts, and the product mechanism is the layout itself.
materials: carbonless paper plies with perforated edges
registration ticks and numbered form fields
options.viewport: A large order form fills the frame: Softlligence headline in printed form type, a stepped stack of four plies peeking out below, each tab labelled with a product name and its real tagline. One primary action, 'Open live demo' or 'Book a demo', sits as the form's submit field. Nav is a form header row.
options.risk: Reads as paperwork nostalgia if ply colours get pastel-cute; it must stay as strict and dense as a real form. Needs care with mobile, where plies stack as numbered sheets.

raised.raise: Everything registers to one measured grid, so the plies align edge to edge like a printed form.
Exactly four ply colours, one per product, plus one ink; hierarchy by borders and inversion, not extra colours.
Colour is reserved for state: a ply only tints when its product is selected or has a live demo.

options.verdicts: All six challengers declined on audience identification.

options.label: The Industrial Parts Catalogue
options.lineage: Swiss-style industrial catalogues and spec sheets (Siemens, Braun, Festo)
options.thesis: A strict modular grid, white ground, one signal red, product photography-style cut-outs and spec tables: the site as a catalogue of four numbered products with part-number-style codes.
options.viewport: Left rail with the Softlligence wordmark and a numbered product index (01 ERP, 02 CRM, 03 MIS, 04 Inventory); main field shows the lead product's spec table and one red action.
options.risk: Most familiar option; this is where many enterprise sites land. It is credible but could be mistaken for a template.

options.label: Colour Chord Canopy
options.lineage: translucent silk banners over a courtyard
options.case: Fuses beautifully but obscures what the products do.
options.kept: Overlap as a labelled joint state; echoed by plies showing through each other.

options.label: Alphabet Storm
options.case: Loses on clarity: buyers must read a plain offer.
options.kept: One monumental grotesk used as the headline voice.

options.label: Kaiju Broadcast Alert
options.case: Alarm register fights a sober enterprise buyer.

options.label: Game Boy Four-Shade Field
options.case: A game metaphor undermines enterprise trust.
options.kept: Exactly four tones, one per product.

options.label: Hand-drawn Zine
options.case: This is the off-tone playfulness the critique flagged.

options.label: Oscilloscope Signal Bench
options.case: Instrument costume for buyers who are not engineers.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: Clean enterprise SaaS: white ground, navy type, one blue accent, product screenshots in a hero, logo row, feature grid.
canonCard.viewport: Headline, sub-copy, two buttons and a dashboard screenshot.
